texts.facts: The present Detailed Accident Report arises out of road accident that occurred on 12.08.2018, in which one Mukul Singh (aged about 26 years) allegedly suffered Mukul Singh (Dar) vs Krishan Kumar (92/18 Dfc) on 28 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109443083/ 1 grievous injury. 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 12.08.2018 vide DD no.7A dated 12.08.2018 at 6.45 AM, it was informed that an accident had taken place under the South Extension flyover. ASI Anil Kumar reached on the spot i.e. Ring Road Mool Chand underpass where a taxi i.e. TATA Summo bearing no.HR47D-6544 and truck traula Loaded No.RJ-32-GB-7999 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) were found in accidental condition. Vide DD no.9A, was informed that the injured had been shifted to Moolchand hospital and found not fit for giving statement. IO prepared site plan and sent the TATA Sumo and Truck Trolla for inspection. During investigation, IO recorded statement of one Raj Singh who was travelling alongwith injured in the said TATA Sumo. He stated that on 12.08.2018, after finishing duties, he alongwith injured was returning in company cab which was being driven by one Kuldeep, after finishing their duty. At around 6.30 AM the cab MACT NO.17/19 Mukul Singh vs. Krishan Kumar & ors. P.No. 2 Of 21 ss Digitally signed by CHARU CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.08.28 16:58:00 +0530 hit against the offending vehicle which was parked on the wrong side of the road without any indication or lights due to the impact all the three occupants of the car persons including the driver sustained grievous injuries. 3. An FIR no.092/18, dated 12.08.2018 was registered u/s 279,337 of IPC PS-Defence Colony. Matter was investigated and a chargesheet u/s 279/337/338 of IPC was filed before concerned criminal court while DAR was filed before this Tribunal. 4. Respondent no.1 is the driver, respondent no.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle. Respondent no.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle. 5. Respondent no.1 and 2 did not file any reply despite opportunity. Respondent no.3/insurance company filed a legal offer which was declined by the petitioner. In its reply/written statement, respondent no.3 has denied its liability to compensate the petitioner on the ground that the respondent no.1 was not holding a valid driving licence at the time of accident. 6. Vide order dated 21.11.2019, following issues were framed. 1. Whether the injured Mukul Singh suffered injuries in a road traffic accident dated 12.08.2018 involving vehicle bearing no.RJ-32GB-7999 driven by R1 and owned by R2 and insured with R3 due to rash and negligent driving of R-1?OPP. OPP. 3. Relief. Mukul Singh (Dar) vs Krishan Kumar (92/18 Dfc) on 28 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109443083/ 2 MACT NO.17/19 Mukul Singh vs. Krishan Kumar & ors. P.No. 3 Of 21 ss Digitally signed by CHARU CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.08.28 16:58:04 +0530 7. In order to prove his claim, petitioner/injured Mukul Singh led evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He deposed on the lines of the DAR. He stated that on 12.08.2018 at about 6.30 AM he was returning home in his office cab. When he reached at Moolchand Flyover underpass, New Delhi, the offending vehicle bearing no. RJ-32GB-7999 was found wrongly parked on the road by respondent no.1 without parking light and indicator, in careless and negligent manner. Due to this, the vehicle in which PW-1 was travelling collided with the offending vehicle from behind. As a result, PW-1 sustained injuries and was shifted to Moolchand hospital where his MLC bearing no.6579/18 was prepared. He remained admitted from 12.08.2018 to 31.08.2018 and again admitted on 06.09.2018 and discharged on 11.09.2018. He deposed that he used to work in SBI Card and Payment Services at Gurugram and was earning Rs.20,000/- p.m. He deposed that due to the accident, he could not resume his services. He has spent Rs.62,500/- on his medical treatment, Rs.1,00,000/- on special diet and Rs.1,50,000/- on conveyance and Rs.3,00,000/- on attendant. He relied upon documents i.e. Aadhar card as Ex.PW-1/1, MLC as Ex.PW-1/2, Discharge summary as Ex.PW-1/3, Medical treatment and OPD card as Ex.PW-1/4, Medical bills as Ex.PW-1/5, DAR as Ex.PW-1/6. He was duly cross - examined by learned counsel for insurance company/respondent no.3. No evidence was led by the respondents despite opportunity. As the matter is more than five years old, court has proceeded to decided adjudicate the claim on the basis of material on record and evidence adduced. Accordingly, issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents. Issue no. 2 Whether the claimant is entitled to any MACT NO.17/19 Mukul Singh vs. Krishan Kumar & ors. Total Compensation Rs.18,16,891/- Interest Simple interest @7.5% p.a. from the date of filing of DAR till actual realization of Award amount/ compensation.
texts.arguments: Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & Ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. 10. In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 12. It may further be noted that in Cholamandalam Insurance Company vs. Kamlesh, 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if the driver of the offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. 15. As regards the quantum of compensation, this court is governed by the law laid down by Hon'le Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680. The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. 16.6. Observation of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rajkumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. is quoted hereunder: The State Bank of India, Saket Courts, Delhi is MACT NO.17/19 Mukul Singh vs. Krishan Kumar & ors. 28. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: " ......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". But if the Tribunal is satisfied for reasons to be stated in writing that the whole or part of the amount is required for expanding an existing business or for purchasing some property for earning a livelihood, the Tribunal can release the whole or part of the amount of compensation to the claimant provided MACT NO.17/19 Mukul Singh vs. Krishan Kumar & ors. P.No. 17 Of 21 ss CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 2025.08.28 16:58:56 +0530 the Tribunal will ensure that the amount is invested for the purpose for which it is demanded and paid. Thus, sufficient discretion has been given to the Tribunal not to insist on investment of the compensation amount in long term fixed deposit and to release even the whole amount in the case Mukul Singh (Dar) vs Krishan Kumar (92/18 Dfc) on 28 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109443083/ 12 of literate persons.
